_comment: USER-FACING highlights for the release named by `version`, published to the website as
🔴 UPDATE THIS IN THE PR THAT PREPARES A RELEASE, BEFORE TAGGING. The `guard` job fails
the release when `version` does not match the tag, deliberately and as the FIRST job —
so a forgotten update costs nothing but a re-run, rather than publishing last release's
highlights against this release's version. Confidently wrong is worse than absent, and
this file is the one part of the manifest a machine cannot derive.
WRITE FOR SOMEONE DECIDING WHETHER TO UPGRADE, not for someone reading the commit log.
The changelog is already generated from commit subjects and is right there in the release
notes; repeating `fix(events): give payload rows and anchors identities of their own` here
adds nothing. Say what changed for the person running the platform.
Keep it to a handful of lines. This renders in a download menu and a docs banner, not in
a document — a fifteen-item list is a changelog wearing a different hat.
`breaking` drives an automatic warning on the website and in the docs. Set it true when an
upgrade is not a plain `helm upgrade`, and say so in the first highlight.
highlights: Upgradeable in place: the first release since v0.8.5 that a plain helm upgrade can reach.
Deleting a tenant now erases its data — relational, telemetry, broker, object and key-value stores, and the running rule engine.
A deleted tenant's token is held before reuse, so a new tenant cannot inherit its predecessor's data.
The console shows deletion progress and history, with a per-store record of what was erased.
A device can no longer take over another tenant's MQTT session by reusing its client id.
The console refuses to publish a dashboard whose widgets are misconfigured.
